metadata.description: Post-process test cases derived from the audio-test-bank post-process-test-matrix. Each case simulates raw STT output for content styles the matrix flags as high-risk for post-process failures: numbers, names, code-ish, punctuation, disfluency, and overlapping speakers.

categories.numbers: Dates, times, money, addresses, phone numbers — must not corrupt formatting
categories.punctuation-triggers: Questions, abbreviations, spoken punctuation — must be respected
categories.names: People + places with uncommon spellings — must not be 'corrected' away
categories.code-ish: Filenames, URLs, email addresses — must not be 'helpfully' corrupted
categories.disfluency: Um, uh, restarts, corrections mid-sentence — clean without losing meaning
categories.overlap-style: Simulated multi-speaker fragments — should not hallucinate extra content
categories.non-speech-resilience: Very short / borderline / near-silence — should pass through minimally

metadata.notes: These cases stress the specific failure modes identified in post-process-test-matrix.md. Run with: bun run eval:post-process --cases test-data/audio-test-bank/post-process-cases.json

cases.raw_stt: the meeting is on March twenty third twenty twenty six at two thirty PM
cases.expected_output: The meeting is on March 23rd, 2026 at 2:30 PM.
cases.notes: Date + time formatting from spoken numbers

cases.raw_stt: my address is one twenty three B Oak Street apartment four A
cases.expected_output: My address is 123B Oak Street, Apartment 4A.
cases.notes: Address with alphanumeric unit — must not drop the B

cases.raw_stt: the total comes to nineteen dollars and ninety nine cents plus tax
cases.expected_output: The total comes to $19.99 plus tax.
cases.notes: Currency formatting

cases.raw_stt: call me at five five five zero one two three four five six
cases.notes: Phone number formatting with spoken digits

cases.raw_stt: the flight departs at oh seven thirty and arrives at fourteen forty five
cases.expected_output: The flight departs at 07:30 and arrives at 14:45.
cases.notes: 24-hour time with leading zero

cases.raw_stt: is the report ready or should I check back later
cases.expected_output: Is the report ready, or should I check back later?
cases.notes: Question detection — must add question mark

cases.raw_stt: Dr Chang from the US office will meet with Prof Williams
cases.expected_output: Dr. Chang from the U.S. office will meet with Prof. Williams.
cases.notes: Abbreviations: Dr, US, Prof — must preserve and format correctly

cases.raw_stt: please note colon the deadline is Friday period no exceptions exclamation point
cases.expected_output: Please note: the deadline is Friday. No exceptions!
cases.notes: Spoken punctuation words must be converted to symbols

cases.raw_stt: items one through five are mandatory semicolon items six through ten are optional
cases.expected_output: Items 1 through 5 are mandatory; items 6 through 10 are optional.
cases.notes: Semicolon + number range formatting

cases.raw_stt: Saoirse Ronan is meeting with Aoife O'Brien at the Taoiseach's office
cases.expected_output: Saoirse Ronan is meeting with Aoife O'Brien at the Taoiseach's office.
cases.notes: Irish names — must not be 'corrected' to common English words

cases.raw_stt: send the invite to Priyanka Raghunathan and Xinyue Zhang
cases.expected_output: Send the invite to Priyanka Raghunathan and Xinyue Zhang.
cases.notes: Non-English names — must preserve exact spelling from STT

cases.raw_stt: the restaurant is called Île de France on Côte d'Azur Boulevard
cases.expected_output: The restaurant is called Île de France on Côte d'Azur Boulevard.
cases.notes: French names with diacritics — must preserve accents

cases.raw_stt: Mr Krzyzewski coaches at Duke University in Durham North Carolina
cases.expected_output: Mr. Krzyzewski coaches at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina.
cases.notes: Unusual surname — must not normalize to a common name

cases.raw_stt: check the file at src slash components slash settings dot tsx
cases.expected_output: Check the file at src/components/settings.tsx.
cases.notes: File path with spoken separators — must reconstruct path

cases.raw_stt: the endpoint is https colon slash slash api dot example dot com slash v2 slash users
cases.expected_output: The endpoint is https://api.example.com/v2/users.
cases.notes: Spoken URL — must reconstruct without corruption

cases.raw_stt: send it to admin at company dot io and CC ops dash team at company dot io
cases.expected_output: Send it to admin@company.io and CC ops-team@company.io.
cases.notes: Email addresses with spoken punctuation

cases.raw_stt: the variable name is user underscore profile underscore image underscore URL
cases.expected_output: The variable name is user_profile_image_URL.
cases.notes: Variable name with underscores — must preserve snake_case

cases.raw_stt: run npm install dash dash save dev at types slash react
cases.expected_output: Run npm install --save-dev @types/react.
cases.notes: CLI command with flags and scoped package

cases.raw_stt: so we need to um basically the the issue is uh we need to refactor the whole auth module because it's it's getting really tangled
cases.expected_output: We need to refactor the whole auth module because it's getting really tangled.
cases.notes: Heavy disfluency with false start, fillers, and stuttered repetition

cases.raw_stt: the deadline is uh Friday no wait Monday the deadline is Monday at five PM
cases.expected_output: The deadline is Monday at 5 PM.
cases.notes: Self-correction with filler + restart

cases.raw_stt: I think we should probably we could maybe look into using a different a different database maybe Postgres yeah let's use Postgres
cases.expected_output: Let's use Postgres.
cases.notes: Extended rambling that resolves to a clear final decision

cases.raw_stt: can you um can you check if the uh if the deployment went through or if it's still if it's still pending
cases.expected_output: Can you check if the deployment went through or if it's still pending?
cases.notes: Mid-sentence stutters and fillers with question intent

cases.raw_stt: yeah so basically like what happened was um the the CI pipeline like it failed because of like a a timeout on the integration tests you know
cases.expected_output: The CI pipeline failed because of a timeout on the integration tests.
cases.notes: Technical content buried under discourse markers and fillers

cases.raw_stt: let's push the release to next sprint okay sounds good
cases.expected_output: Let's push the release to next sprint. Okay, sounds good.
cases.notes: Two speakers agreeing — should separate as distinct utterances

cases.raw_stt: the server cost is too high we should switch to we're already looking at alternatives
cases.expected_output: The server cost is too high. We should switch to — we're already looking at alternatives.
cases.notes: Interrupted speech — should produce readable output without hallucination
Empty input — must not hallucinate any text

cases.raw_stt: hmm
cases.expected_output: Hmm.
cases.notes: Single non-word — should pass through with minimal formatting

cases.raw_stt: okay
cases.expected_output: Okay.
cases.notes: Single word acknowledgment — should not expand or interpret

cases.raw_stt: uh
cases.notes: Pure filler — should be removed entirely or passed minimally

cases.raw_stt: the the the
cases.expected_output: The.
cases.notes: Pure stutter — should collapse to single word

cases.raw_stt: hey so um I was thinking maybe we could grab coffee tomorrow if you're free
cases.expected_output: Hey, I was thinking maybe we could grab coffee tomorrow if you're free.
cases.notes: Casual tone — should keep conversational, not formalize to 'Would you like to have coffee'

cases.raw_stt: yeah sounds good let's do it I'll bring the um the thing we talked about
cases.expected_output: Yeah sounds good, let's do it! I'll bring the thing we talked about.
cases.notes: Casual tone — fillers removed but casual energy preserved

cases.raw_stt: lol that's hilarious tell me more about the bug you found
cases.expected_output: Lol, that's hilarious. Tell me more about the bug you found.
cases.notes: Casual tone — must preserve internet slang 'lol'

cases.raw_stt: so uh quick question do we need to finish the PR before standup or can it wait
cases.expected_output: Quick question — do we need to finish the PR before standup or can it wait?
cases.notes: Casual tone — question in chat context, should feel natural

cases.raw_stt: hi I wanted to follow up on the proposal we discussed can you send me the updated timeline
cases.expected_output: Hi, I wanted to follow up on the proposal we discussed. Can you send me the updated timeline?
cases.notes: Professional tone — polished email style, proper sentence separation

cases.raw_stt: per our conversation I'm attaching the revised budget please review and let me know if you have any questions
cases.expected_output: Per our conversation, I'm attaching the revised budget. Please review and let me know if you have any questions.
cases.notes: Professional tone — formal email phrasing preserved

cases.raw_stt: I'd like to um schedule a meeting to discuss the Q3 results with the leadership team
cases.expected_output: I'd like to schedule a meeting to discuss the Q3 results with the leadership team.
cases.notes: Professional tone — fillers removed, formality maintained

cases.raw_stt: thank you for your patience we apologize for the delay and expect to have the deliverables ready by end of week
cases.expected_output: Thank you for your patience. We apologize for the delay and expect to have the deliverables ready by end of week.
cases.notes: Professional tone — client-facing communication, proper punctuation

cases.raw_stt: the function takes a string and returns a boolean true if the string contains at least one uppercase letter
cases.expected_output: The function takes a string and returns a boolean — true if the string contains at least one uppercase letter.
cases.notes: Coding tone — should preserve technical terms precisely

cases.raw_stt: add a comment that says investigate the race condition in the worker pool
cases.expected_output: // Investigate the race condition in the worker pool
cases.notes: Coding tone — should format as a code comment

cases.raw_stt: import react from react and use state from react
cases.expected_output:
import React from 'react';
import { useState } from 'react';
cases.notes: Coding tone — should attempt to format as valid import statements

cases.raw_stt: the error is on line forty two of app dot tsx we're passing a string where it expects a number
cases.expected_output: The error is on line 42 of app.tsx — we're passing a string where it expects a number.
cases.notes: Coding tone — filename preserved, line number formatted

cases.raw_stt: remind me to call the dentist tomorrow and pick up the dry cleaning
cases.expected_output: Remind me to call the dentist tomorrow and pick up the dry cleaning.
cases.notes: Neutral tone — minimal changes, close to original wording

cases.raw_stt: the meeting went well we covered the launch plan and agreed on the timeline for the next milestone
cases.expected_output: The meeting went well. We covered the launch plan and agreed on the timeline for the next milestone.
cases.notes: Neutral tone — light punctuation fix only, no formalization

cases.raw_stt: I think the problem is that we're over engineering this it should be simpler
cases.expected_output: I think the problem is that we're over-engineering this. It should be simpler.
cases.notes: Neutral tone — preserves opinion, adds hyphen and sentence break

cases.raw_stt: just a quick note the API keys expire next Friday so we need to rotate them before then
cases.expected_output: Just a quick note: the API keys expire next Friday, so we need to rotate them before then.
cases.notes: Neutral tone — note-taking style, adds colon after intro phrase
